statements.t: We use proprietary technology to design DNA plasmids, which are small circular DNA molecules that work like software the body’s cells can download to produce specific proteins to target and fight disease.

Subject to further regulatory feedback, we expect a confirmatory study to evaluate the number of surgical interventions required over at least three years, following completion of treatment, and compare this to an appropriate external control group or scientifically justified threshold.
We expect to submit a draft protocol for this confirmatory study by the end of 2026 as required by the FDA, with the goal of aligning on a final protocol by mid-2027.
We expect to make VOCERYQ available to order and ship in approximately 60 days from approval and anticipate full field deployment during the first quarter of 2027.
We also expect insurers that cover approximately 80% of patients in the US to have policies in place for coverage within nine months of approval, based on our Payer research to date.
In addition to our U.S. regulatory activities, we plan to submit an application for conditional marketing authorization for VOCERYQ in Europe before the end of 2026.
Our field teams will aim to engage both of these customer segments, and overall, our field footprint will aim to cover about 90% of RRP patient potential.
Our field organization is expected to include 20 territories with Key Account Managers, reimbursement specialists, and dedicated payer support capabilities deployed across those territories.

We expect our device and plasmid manufacturing network to be prepared to meet anticipated demand, with current inventory and capacity available to support the first year of launch through at least 2027.

We anticipate VOCERYQ to be priced at approximately $115,000 per dose, or $460,000 for the complete four-dose treatment series, which is consistent with the previously approved immunotherapy to treat adults with RRP.

INO-5401 encodes for our Synthetic Consensus antigens of hTERT, WT1, and PSMA, which are antigens the National Cancer Institute has highlighted as important targets and designated as high priorities for cancer immunotherapy development.

Other products in our development pipeline include INO-3112, a DNA immunotherapy candidate targeting HPV-16/-18 combined with a DNA plasmid encoding for human IL-12 as an immune activator, for the treatment of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, or OPSCC, a type of head and neck cancer commonly known as throat cancer.
We have not generated any revenues from the sale of any products, and we do not expect to generate any material revenues until we successfully commercialize VOCERYQ.

We expect to continue to incur substantial operating losses in the future due to our commitment to our research and development programs, the funding of preclinical studies, clinical trials and regulatory activities and the costs of selling, general and administrative activities.
We utilize a labor reporting system to record employee compensation on a project-by-project basis.
As of September 30, 2026, we had an accumulated deficit of $1.9 billion, and we expect to continue to operate at a loss for the near term.
Our accumulated deficit is expected to increase as we incur expenses to commercialize VOCERYQ and continue our research and development efforts.
We anticipate that additional financing will be required to commercialize VOCERYQ, conduct post-approval clinical development activities and complete the development of our other product candidates.
If our other product candidates receive regulatory approval, we will also need additional funding to market and sell those products and related equipment.
We expect our cash runway to extend into late fourth quarter 2027, without giving effect to any further capital raising activities that we may undertake.
We expect to continue to rely on outside sources of financing to meet our capital needs and we may never achieve positive cash flow.
We expect to satisfy these obligations from existing cash over the next twelve months.
